parole.testo: From Middle Ukrainian августъ (avhust), август (avhust), аугоустъ (auhust), from Byzantine Greek Αὔγουστος (Aúgoustos), from Latin Augustus.
From Byzantine Greek αὐτοκρατία (autokratía). Compare Russian автокра́тия (avtokrátija), Belarusian аўтакра́тыя (awtakrátyja), Polish autokracja.

parole.significato: alphabet (an ordered set of letters used in a language)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Byzantine Greek ἀλφάβητον (alphábēton), from ἄλφα (álpha, “alpha”) and βήτα (bḗta, “beta”) (the names of the first two letters in the Greek alphabet). Doublet of альфабе́т (alʹfabét). Compare 17th-century Ukrainian алфавитъ (alfavyt), Belarusian алфаві́т (alfavít), Russian алфави́т (al

parole.significato: leap, bissextile (referring to leap years, leap days, etc.)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic високостьныи (visokostĭnyi), from високостъ (visokostŭ, “leap day”), from Byzantine Greek βίσεξτος (bísextos), from Late Latin bissextus, from Latin bisextus. Compare Russian високо́сный (visokósnyj), Belarusian высако́сны (vysakósny).

parole.significato: a dish of boiled wheat and honey served at Christmas, New Year's, Epiphany, funerals, equivalent to колива/koliva serve…
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian кꙋтьѧ (kutʹja), from Old East Slavic кꙋтьꙗ (kutĭja), from Byzantine Greek κουκκιά (koukkiá, “broad beans”), whence also Old Church Slavonic коуциꙗ (kucija). Compare ко́ливо (kólyvo).

parole.significato: legion (superior combat unit of the Roman army)
parole.testo: From Old Ruthenian легеонъ (leheon), borrowed from Byzantine Greek λεγιών (legiṓn). Ultimately from Latin legō (“to gather”) + -іон (-ion).

parole.significato: robe, gown (a long loose outer garment, often signifying honorary stature or professional status)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Byzantine Greek μάντιον (mántion) (or μαντίον (mantíon)), from Latin mantum. Compare Russian ма́нтия (mántija), Belarusian ма́нтыя (mántyja).

parole.significato: sexton, sacristan, vestry keeper; the parishioner who acts as the priest's main assistant during the Liturgy
parole.testo: Clipping of парамона́р (paramonár), from Byzantine Greek παραμοναριος (paramonarios), from παραμένω (paraménō, “stand beside”).
Borrowed from Byzantine Greek παλάτιον (palátion), from Latin palātium.
Inherited from Old Ruthenian смарагдъ (smarahd), from Old East Slavic смарагдъ, измарагдъ (smaragdŭ, izmaragdŭ), from Byzantine Greek σμάραγδος (smáragdos).

parole.significato: a student of a theological school; primary and middle school student of the Kyiv Collegium (later Academy)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian спудей (spudej), from Byzantine Greek σπουδαῖος (spoudaîos). Compare Greek σπουδή (spoudí, “study”).

From Old East Slavic субота (subota), from Byzantine Greek *σάμβατον (*sámbaton), from Ancient Greek σάββατα (sábbata), from Aramaic שַׁבְּתָא (šabbǝtā) or Hebrew שַׁבָּת (šabbāṯ). Cognates include Russian суббо́та (subbóta), Belarusian субо́та (subóta), Old Church Slavonic сѫбота (sǫbota), Bulgaria
